text:
sam: kicking off a small canary for a p95-driven queue budget change. goal: keep p95 <= 140ms for `chat` route while improving throughput/cost. rolling 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 18h unless rollback triggers hit.

lee: quick note from profiling: we saw kernel handoff at microbatch size 8 -> 16 spike for long seqs. if we lower token_budget target below 48 tokens, we avoid kernel B and stay on kernel A (much better tail).

anya: observed KV hitrate dip in last test when token budgets tightened. warmup + prefix caching for chat system prompts reduced miss rate by ~4%. recommend enabling prefetch for route-tier=enterprise in canary.

runtime-bot: deploy event: canary-started by @sam. config snippet: 
```json
{
  "routes": ["chat"],
  "route_tiers": ["standard","enterprise"],
  "token_budget_targets": {"standard": 64, "enterprise": 96},
  "rollout": [1,5,20],
  "slo_p95_ms": 140,
  "rollback_on_p95_exceed_ms": 200
}
```

taylor: initial metrics @ +15m: p95=152ms, qps +12%, kv_hit=0.78. most of p95 increase from a few outlier requests with seq>1024. logs: `kernel_switch: B at batch_sz=16`.

lee: suggestion: set dynamic kernel preference rule: prefer kernel A if expected_batch_tokens <= 1024; fallback to B only if microbatching yields net benefit. add hysteresis to avoid flip-flop.

anya: also recommend a short-lived prefetch job for active prefixes during canary start. command we've used: `./prefetcher --route chat --window 10m --parallel 8` — this raised kv_hit to 0.84 in lab.

ops: rollback criteria acked: p95 > 200ms for 10m OR kv_hit drop > 8% sustained for 15m. alerting configured. @sam please confirm thresholds. :white_check_mark:

sam: confirmed. will pause at 5% if p95 > 180ms for 5m to investigate. otherwise advance. starting 1% window now, will post updates at each stage.

runtime-bot: canary progress: stage 1 (1%) complete @ +1h, observed p95 median 148ms, tail 168ms, kv_hit steady at 0.80. advancing to 5%.

sam: advancing to 5% now. keeping kernel-preference rule and prefetch on for enterprise tier. tagging @lee to watch kernel-switch logs and @anya for KV metrics.
